newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt trades higher, likely to stay in range.
newsitem.headline: German debt trades higher, likely to stay in range.

text.p: German debt closed trading higher on Friday and was expected to trade in a narrow range during the next week as most European markets will be closed for several days for the Christmas holiday.
Shortly before the close, the March Bund futures contract was trading up 10 basis points at 100.42, having traded in a range of 100.40-100.72 during the session.

At the same time the April 2006 cash bond was trading at 102.95 compared with Thursday's close of 102.82. Few dealers see significant trading impulses next week and said they would be very surprised if the market broke out of its range.
"Next week I expect we will trade in a range somewhere between 100.20 und 101.00," one dealer said.
Dealers said that most of the day's action happened in the futures market and was largely impacted by trading in the U.S.
Gains in Treasuries at first helped the market climb before it stabilised at higher levels.
In the late afternoon, dealers squared positions after higher U.S. prices were not able to help the market break out of its range.
